names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 14 octombrie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Οκτωβρίου, «Οσία Παρασκευή η Νέα η «Επιβατηνή»», with the rank word left off.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's day line, «Прп. Параскевы-Петки Сербской», with the rank word left off; one of its lives heads her «Преподобная Параскева-Петка Сербская, Болгарская» and the index page «Преподобная Параскева Сербская». The Russian calls her Serbian where the Romanian calls her of Iași and the Greek of Epivates, and the three mean the same woman.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 14. октобар ст. ст., „Преп. Петка – Параскева.“ — «Преп.» is the `venerable` grade this corpus keeps in `types` and comes off. The heading then gives TWO bare forms for the one woman, joined by the book’s own dash, and section 6 allows one: «Петка», the Serbian vernacular half, is stored, because «Параскева» is already in this folder in Greek, in Romanian and inside the Russian form «Параскева-Петка Сербская», and because «Петка» is the form the day’s verse uses throughout. The whole heading is quoted in the attestation, so the half not stored is on the folder. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for both halves.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «Sfânta Cuvioasă Parascheva a trăit pe pământ în prima jumătate a veacului al XI-lea.» The page gives no year for her birth or her death; the interval is that statement and nothing narrower. days.pravoslavie.ru agrees and says no more: its day line gives «Прп. Параскевы-Петки Сербской (XI)» and both of the lives its index page links put the family «жившей в XI веке в селении Епиват».

feast.note: Her name page lists one other day, «30 августа (Серб.)», the synaxis of the Serbian saints. One row per church is the schema, so the August day is recorded here and she does not render on it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 14 октября ст. ст. — «Прп. Параскевы-Петки Сербской (XI).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the icon standing immediately before her line, «Совершается служба со славословием» — the service with the Great Doxology. It is a great line's own icon and reaches no further; the day's other icon is the plain service and stands before the four martyrs of Milan.

attestations.note: The same woman, and the Russian proves it rather than her name doing so: its lives put her relics «в соборном храме в Яссах», in the cathedral at Iași, which is where this folder's Romanian name comes from, and her birth at Epivates between Silistra and Constantinople, which is where the Greek's «Επιβατηνή» comes from. What it adds is the verse that pierced her «как стрела», like an arrow — Matthew 16:24 — the clothes given to the poor and the grief that brought her from her own family, the Jordan valley where she laboured to a great age, and the angel who two years before the end told her to go home.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 14 octombrie — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Parascheva de la Iași»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Οκτωβρίου — «Οσία Παρασκευή η Νέα η «Επιβατηνή»»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same menologion day the folder already keeps for the Romanian church, and the entry is the same woman: of Epivatai near Selymbria in Thrace, who kept a church at Herakleia of Pontus for five years, lived in a women's monastery in the Holy Land, and died at Kallikrateia in south-eastern Thrace in the church of the Holy Apostles. The folder's own life, from doxologia, names Epivata and the same course. The page gives no year and no century, so no `dates` object is proposed and the folder's own `death` is left alone. It prints no hymn; what it does add is who wrote her service and her life — «Την ακολουθία της συνέγραψε ο Συρίγος Μελέτιος, τον δε βιο της ο Eυθύμιος ο Aρχιεπίσκοπος Tορνόβου». **Not to be confused with the Οσιομάρτυς Παρασκευή of the same day's «Ανάμνηση θαύματος … εν Xίω» (/2751/), which is a commemoration of a miracle of 1442 and belongs to the other Paraskeve.** No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 27.10.2026 (14. октобар ст. ст.) — „Преп. Петка – Параскева.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, ONE WOMAN UNDER TWO NAMES. The heading is quoted whole, with the closing full stop the Prologue prints, which is BRIEF-SERBIAN section 4; the dash in it is the book’s own apposition and not a company. THE NAME FORM STORED IS THE FIRST HALF AND THAT IS A READING, NOT A RULE. Section 6 asks for one sr form, the fullest the calendar gives, and bare; this heading gives two bare forms and neither carries an epithet. «Параскева» is the name this folder already holds in Greek (Παρασκευή), in Romanian (Parascheva de la Iași) and inside its Russian form (Параскева-Петка Сербская), so storing it would add nothing; «Петка» is the Serbian vernacular half, the half the Russian form itself records as the Serbian one, and the form Bishop Nikolai’s verse uses throughout — «О предивна светитељко, света Петко!» — so that is what is stored. The heading is quoted whole in this row, so the other half is on the folder and visible. THE BOOK CALLS HER SERBIAN. «Ова славна светитељка беше српскога порекла» — of Serbian descent — where the folder’s display name is of Iași, which is where her relics now are, and its Russian form already reads «Сербская». NOTHING IS CHANGED on that: a display name is reserved by section 10 and a reader names a sourced correction rather than making one. `dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THIS BOOK IS THE WIDER READING. The folder holds `death` 1000 to 1050, «first half of the 11th century»; this entry says «Упокојила се у XI столећу», the eleventh century whole, which is WIDER than what the folder already holds. A century that contains the recorded interval neither contradicts it nor narrows it, and widening a folder to a less precise reading would be a loss, so nothing moved. `types` untouched: «Преп.» is the `venerable` this folder holds. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS. The birthplace is given three ways — «у граду Епивату (Пиват, по турски Бојадос, између Силимврије и Цариграда» — between Selymbria and Constantinople. Her parents were WELL-OFF and devout Christians. SHE HAD A BROTHER, Јевтимије, who was tonsured while their parents were still alive and later became the renowned BISHOP OF MADYTOS: that is `euthymius-of-madytos`, whose own folder is named by the Romanian calendar as «Eftimie, fratele Cuvioasei Parascheva de la Iași», so the identification is read on both sides and the two folders now relate one another. He gets no row of his own — he is not named in this heading — only the reciprocal row the prose owes him. After her parents died she went first to Constantinople and then TO THE WILDERNESS OF JORDAN, where she struggled into old age. IN OLD AGE AN ANGEL OF GOD APPEARED TO HER with the order that sent her home — «Остави пустињу, и врати се у твоје отечество: потребно је да тамо предаш своје тело земљи, а душом да се преселиш Господу» — and she obeyed the voice from heaven, left the wilderness she loved, lived two more years at Epivates in unceasing fast and prayer, and died there. THE ROUTE OF HER RELICS IS GIVEN IN FULL and no other book read for this folder gives it: Constantinople, then Trnovo, then Constantinople again, then Belgrade, and now Iași in Romania. AND THERE IS AN AGIASMA: a holy spring of hers in the city of Belgrade which heals the sick who come to it with faith in God and love for her. No `locations` all the same: a city named in four translations is not a coordinate. THE FORM IS FREE: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Петка» and for «Параскева» alike. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion — the day’s verse is about her and is Bishop Nikolai’s own, and section 3 keeps it out of `hymns`.
